cells.tense: The pen is in your hand right now and you are writing with it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are already steering and say out loud, to no one, that you are the one steering it.
cells.core:
You point at one thing and let the rest go, and you can feel it happening while you do it. That is what direction is — not force, just attention landing where you meant it to land. This is not a mood that comes and goes. It is doing its work in this minute, and it is holding.

What is in front of you is finishing something, and finishing is not the same as stopping. You have enough hold to let a thing be done and still walk out of the room. That hold is what makes letting go possible. If you want to feed it, feed it from the same place: keep the shape a little longer than feels necessary, then open your hand.
cells.sheetLine: You are the one pointing, and the pointing is working.
cells.verb: pointing at one thing and claiming it
cells.place: at the edge of something finished, before the next step

cells.tense: Your hand is already on a door that has not been built yet.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you keep trying to make happen this week and let it sit undone for a day without touching it.
cells.core:
You are gripping a shape that has not arrived. A conversation turns into a chance to steer it, a silence into a problem to fix, and the grip has gotten tighter than the thing it was for. You are writing an ending for a story that is still being told.

The cost is the thing itself. When you force a finish, the finish arrives before the thing was ready to hold it. Seeing the whole pattern from where you stand is real — but seeing it does not mean running it. Let one piece stay unfinished on purpose. What you release, you get to watch instead of carrying.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.ask: Do one small thing today that nobody asked for and tell one person you did it — no explanation, just the fact of it.
cells.core:
The pen is down and has been down. You know what you would point at if picking were on the table, and it is not, so the question stops there. What is gone is not the ability to point. It is the belief that pointing changes anything.

You do not need to push yourself into the hollow place. What pulls the current back is doing the thing you are already made of, without needing it to prove anything. Shine because it is what you do, not to light the room. The direction is still in you. It just needs somewhere small to land today.

cells.tense: You are already writing in a room you think you only walked into.
cells.ask: Catch one thing this week you called 'just how it goes' and write down whose choice it actually was.
cells.core:
You are steering and you are calling it momentum. The direction is real — the shape of the day, the things that get finished, the ones that do not — and you describe all of it as if it were happening to you. Habit has taken the pen and you are signing with it.

Nothing is wrong with the writing. The trouble is that you cannot choose differently while you believe there is nothing to choose. Look at one thing you did today that felt inevitable. It had a moment where someone decided, and that someone has your hands. What you are is already shining through it. Say so, and the next move gets easier.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's direction is 'conscious' in the balanced cell — the record cannot show they have noticed their own choosing rather than inherited it. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not choosing at all, things just happen' and the balanced read would miss them entirely. The ask still works if the read is wrong because pointing at one thing and claiming it changes nothing about whether the read was right, and the person gets a fact about their own hand either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'You're the one deciding what gets passed on' — it flatters the reader with authorship the record hasn't established.
